title: Howth Cliff Path
description: One of Dublin's most iconic walks with dramatic sea views, wildflowers, and the smell of salt air the whole way. Ends near the harbour where you can grab fish and chips. About 6km loop.
availabilityNote: Just turn up — exposed to wind, arrive early on weekends

title: Bray to Greystones Cliff Walk
description: A stunning coastal path along the Wicklow cliffs with sea on one side and green hills on the other. DART back from Greystones makes it a perfect one-way trip. Genuinely beautiful.
availabilityNote: Just turn up — DART to Bray to start

title: Ticknock Forest Loop
description: Pine forest trails in the Dublin Mountains with sweeping views over the city and bay on a clear day. Quiet, green, and only 20 mins from the city. Great for clearing your head.
availabilityNote: Just turn up — car park fills on sunny weekends

title: Poolbeg Lighthouse Walk
description: Walk the iconic red-and-white South Bull Wall out into Dublin Bay to the lighthouse. Completely flat, endlessly dramatic, with the city skyline behind you and open sea ahead.
availabilityNote: Just turn up — very exposed, bring layers

title: Phoenix Park Deer Watch
description: One of Europe's largest city parks is home to a herd of wild fallow deer. Wander the grasslands and you'll almost certainly spot them. Bring a coffee and take your time.
availabilityNote: Just turn up — deer are near the Fifteen Acres

title: Sandymount Strand Stroll
description: A wide sandy beach walkway south of the city with views across the bay to Howth. Low tide reveals huge flat sands. Quiet, windswept, and surprisingly meditative.

title: National Botanic Gardens
description: 19,000 plant species across 50 acres in Glasnevin including spectacular Victorian glasshouses you can walk through even in the rain. Peaceful, free, and genuinely underrated.

title: Dun Laoghaire Pier Walk
description: Walk the long granite piers out into Dublin Bay — East Pier is the classic, with views back to the mountains and out to sea. Then coffee in the town after. Reliable, lovely.
searchQuery: Dun Laoghaire pier walk
availabilityNote: Just turn up — DART to Dun Laoghaire

title: Killiney Hill & Vico Bathing Place
description: Hike up Killiney Hill for panoramic views that rival the Bay of Naples, then descend to the Vico Road bathing place for a wild swim off the rocks. Properly special.
availabilityNote: Steep in places — great views at the top

title: St Anne's Park, Raheny
description: A vast and beautiful park in Raheny with rose gardens, woodland trails, and wide open spaces. Far less visited than Phoenix Park but every bit as lovely on a good day.
availabilityNote: Rose Garden best in summer — market some Sundays

title: Bull Island Nature Walk
description: A UNESCO biosphere reserve just 6km from the city centre — sand dunes, a long beach, and incredible birdwatching. Wild and exposed in the best possible way.
searchQuery: Bull Island Dublin nature walk
availabilityNote: Just turn up — take the wooden bridge from Clontarf

title: Djouce Boardwalk & Lough Tay
description: One of Wicklow's most rewarding half-day walks — a boardwalk trail with panoramic views over the Guinness Lake (Lough Tay) and surrounding mountains. Spectacular on a clear day.

title: Malahide Castle Demesne
description: Manicured grounds surrounding a medieval castle north of the city. Wide paths, a walled garden, and a café on site. Peaceful and easy to reach by DART.

title: Seapoint Swim + Sauna
description: Take the plunge in the Irish Sea at Seapoint then warm up in a wood-fired sauna right on the water. Cold, exhilarating, and genuinely addictive once you start.
searchQuery: Seapoint swim sauna Dublin
availabilityNote: Sauna booking recommended — swim is free

title: Forty Foot Swim, Sandycove
description: One of Ireland's most famous sea swimming spots — a rocky inlet at Sandycove where Dubliners have been swimming year-round for centuries. Brace yourself and jump in.
availabilityNote: Just turn up — cold-water swim, take care

title: City Kayaking on the Liffey
description: Guided kayak tour through Dublin's docklands and along the Liffey — a totally different perspective on the city. No experience needed, equipment provided, guides are great craic.

title: SUP at Grand Canal Dock
description: Stand-up paddleboarding on the calm waters of Grand Canal Dock, right in the heart of the city. Easier than it looks, harder than it looks, and absolutely worth it for the laughs.

title: Tandem Cycle in Phoenix Park
description: Hire a tandem bike and wobble your way around one of Europe's biggest city parks. Ridiculous fun, great for photos, and surprisingly hard work. The deer don't care how much you're laughing.

title: Great South Wall Walk
description: Dublin's most dramatic and least-known walk — a 4km granite wall jutting into Dublin Bay, built in the 1730s. Completely exposed to the elements and extraordinary on a clear day.
searchQuery: Great South Wall Dublin walk
availabilityNote: Just turn up — park at Pigeon House Road

title: Vico Road Sea Dip
description: A beautiful cliff-side bathing spot on the Vico Road between Dalkey and Killiney. Small platform, spectacular views, and a swim that feels genuinely earned.
availabilityNote: Steep access — small platform, mind tides

title: Zipit Forest Adventures
description: Tree-top obstacle courses and zip lines in Tibradden Forest in the Dublin Mountains. Brilliant fun, genuinely challenging, and surrounded by great scenery.

title: IMMA — Irish Museum of Modern Art
description: World-class contemporary art in a stunning 17th-century Royal Hospital building. The permanent collection is free, temporary exhibitions are genuinely surprising, and the courtyard is beautiful.
availabilityNote: Collections free — some shows ticketed, late opening Thu

title: Chester Beatty Library
description: Repeatedly voted Europe's best museum — and it's free. An extraordinary collection of manuscripts, books, and art from across Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. Plan to lose two hours.

title: National Gallery of Ireland
description: A genuinely great national collection including Caravaggio, Vermeer, and the largest collection of Irish art in the world — all free. The Millennium Wing alone is worth the visit.

title: Kilmainham Gaol Tour
description: The most important building in modern Irish history — where the leaders of the 1916 Rising were executed. Guided tours are powerful and genuinely moving. Book ahead, it sells out constantly.
availabilityNote: Book ahead — weekends sell out days in advance

title: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
description: An interactive museum telling the story of the Irish diaspora — over 10 million people who left these shores and shaped the world. Unexpectedly emotional and brilliantly designed.

title: National Museum — Archaeology
description: Home to the Ardagh Chalice, the Tara Brooch, and the Bog Bodies — some of the finest Celtic and Viking artefacts in the world. Free, world-class, and reliably impressive.

title: Hugh Lane Gallery
description: A free modern art gallery on Parnell Square with an extraordinary collection including Francis Bacon's reconstructed studio. Quiet, beautiful, and seriously underrated.
availabilityNote: Free entry — Francis Bacon studio is the highlight

title: Science Gallery Dublin
description: Free exhibitions at the intersection of science and art — always thought-provoking, often interactive, and regularly unlike anything else showing in the city. Based at Trinity College.

title: The Little Museum of Dublin
description: A charming, witty museum on St Stephen's Green telling the story of Dublin in the 20th century through donated objects. Guided tours only and they are genuinely brilliant.

title: Marsh's Library
description: Ireland's oldest public library, built in 1707, with original oak bookcases and reading cages where scholars were locked in with rare books. Atmospheric and utterly unique.

title: Glasnevin Cemetery Museum Tour
description: This is where Daniel O'Connell, Michael Collins, and Eamon de Valera are buried. Guided tours bring the whole sweep of Irish history to life in a remarkable way.

title: Dublin Castle State Apartments & Gardens
description: The historic seat of British power in Ireland for 700 years. The State Apartments are surprisingly grand, the gardens are free, and the medieval undercroft is fascinating.

title: Casino Marino
description: One of the finest neoclassical buildings in Europe, hiding 16 rooms behind what looks like a single-roomed temple. A genuine architectural marvel — and almost nobody visits.

title: Dublinia
description: An interactive museum bringing Viking and medieval Dublin to life. Hands-on, well done, and genuinely interesting even without kids. Central location beside Christ Church.

title: Bread 41
description: Widely considered Dublin's best sourdough bakery. The pastries are extraordinary, the coffee is excellent, and the queue moves fast. A perfect morning stop.

title: Sceal Bakery
description: A tiny, beloved bakery in the Liberties doing extraordinary laminated pastries and seasonal bakes. Queue out the door most weekends for good reason — worth every minute.
searchQuery: Sceal Bakery Dublin

title: Clement and Pekoe
description: One of Dublin's finest tea and coffee shops on South William Street — calm, unhurried, and stocked with exceptional loose-leaf teas and single-origin coffees. Perfect for a long slow morning.

title: Two Boys Brew
description: A brilliant neighbourhood coffee shop in Phibsborough with exceptional espresso and some of the best pastries in the city. Relaxed, warm, and always busy for good reason.
searchQuery: Two Boys Brew coffee Dublin Phibsborough

title: Network Cafe
description: A serious specialty coffee shop on Aungier Street with a rotating guest roaster programme. No frills, great coffee, knowledgeable staff. The kind of place you go to actually taste the coffee.
searchQuery: Network Cafe coffee Dublin Aungier Street

title: Firehouse Bakery, Delgany
description: Worth the drive to Wicklow — one of Ireland's best bakeries in a beautiful village setting. Outstanding sourdough, pastries, and coffee. A proper occasion, not just a coffee stop.
availabilityNote: Thu–Sun only — book ahead or queue

title: Kokoro Donuts
description: Dublin's best donuts, full stop. Creative flavours, perfectly executed, and gone by early afternoon most days. Find a bench nearby and eat them immediately.
searchQuery: Kokoro Donuts Dublin
availabilityNote: Sell out fast — go before noon

title: Sheridan's Cheesemongers
description: The best cheese shop in Ireland on South Anne Street. An extraordinary selection of Irish and European cheeses, brilliant staff, and the perfect place to build a picnic.
availabilityNote: Great picnic supplies — pair with a nearby park

title: Bar Pez
description: One of Dublin's best cocktail bars — small, beautifully designed, with a serious but unpretentious drinks list. The kind of place you go for one and leave two hours later very happy.

title: The Peruke and Parlour
description: A wonderfully theatrical cocktail bar on Dawson Street with an extraordinary back bar and inventive drinks list. Baroque decor, serious bartenders, memorable cocktails.

title: The Old Spot Wine Bar
description: A warm, well-stocked wine bar on Bath Avenue with an excellent list by the glass and knowledgeable, unpretentious staff. Great food too. A neighbourhood gem.

title: Against the Grain
description: Dublin's best craft beer bar with an ever-rotating tap list of Irish and international beers. Relaxed, knowledgeable staff, and a great selection of bottles too.
searchQuery: Against the Grain craft beer Dublin Wexford Street

title: Capel Street Natural Wine Bars
description: Capel Street has quietly become Dublin's best street for natural wine — several bars within steps of each other. Wander and find a seat.
searchQuery: natural wine bars Capel Street Dublin

title: Note Restaurant & Wine
description: A stylish, wine-forward restaurant on Fenian Street with an outstanding list by the glass and small plates to match. One of Dublin's best evenings out.

title: IFI Matinee
description: The Irish Film Institute on Eustace Street is one of Europe's great repertory cinemas — showing new releases, classics, and things you won't see anywhere else. The bar and bookshop are excellent too.

title: Lighthouse Cinema
description: A beloved independent cinema on Market Street with a carefully curated programme — art house, documentaries, and the best new releases. Comfortable seats, good popcorn, lovely vibe.

title: Stella Cinema Rathmines
description: A beautifully restored Art Deco cinema in Rathmines with plush seats, cocktails, and a premium experience. The kind of place that makes going to the cinema feel like an event again.

title: Outdoor Cinema Screening
description: Seasonal outdoor cinema screenings pop up across Dublin in summer — parks, rooftops, unexpected spaces. Bring a blanket, get there early, and hope the weather holds.

title: Home Movie Night
description: Sometimes the best answer is to stay in. Pick a film you've both been meaning to watch, get something good to eat, and commit to a proper cinema experience on the couch. No queues.
availabilityNote: Grab snacks, argue about what to watch, enjoy

title: Hodges Figgis Bookshop
description: Dublin's oldest and best bookshop on Dawson Street — four floors of books, a great Irish literature section, and zero pressure to buy anything. Spend an hour or three.

title: Books Upstairs + Café
description: A lovely independent bookshop on D'Olier Street with a café upstairs, excellent staff recommendations, and a strong Irish writing section. A proper bookshop experience.

title: Token Arcade & Board Games
description: A dedicated games venue in Smithfield with retro arcade machines, pinball, board games, and good food. Order drinks, pick something you've never heard of, and settle in.

title: Board Game Café, Blackrock
description: A relaxed board game café in Blackrock with hundreds of games, knowledgeable staff who'll teach you any of them, and good tea and snacks. Easy afternoon sorted.

title: Iveagh Gardens
description: Hidden behind Earlsfort Terrace, most Dubliners have never been. Fountains, a rustic grotto, yew mazes, and wide lawns — usually quiet. One of the best spots in the city on a good day.

title: Merrion Square Park
description: A beautiful Georgian park in the heart of Dublin with sculpture, wide paths, and the famous Oscar Wilde statue. On Sundays local artists display work along the railings.
availabilityNote: Art market on Sundays along the railings

title: George's Street Arcade
description: Dublin's Victorian covered market with vintage stalls, record shops, bookstalls, tarot readers, and a great food hall. A proper Dublin institution worth an unhurried browse.
availabilityNote: Eclectic stalls — dry on rainy days

title: Botanic Gardens Glasshouses
description: The Victorian glasshouses at the National Botanic Gardens are warm, plant-filled, and open even in the rain. A perfect slow hour with no agenda required.
availabilityNote: Warm and peaceful — great in rain

title: St Stephen's Green
description: Grab a coffee, find a bench, and do absolutely nothing for an hour. Watch the ducks, read a book, let the city happen around you. Sometimes that's enough.
availabilityNote: Busy on sunny days — benches and ducks

title: Picnic in Phoenix Park
description: Grab supplies from a good deli, find a spot near the Papal Cross or by the lake, and sit in one of Europe's great city parks. Simple, cheap, and hard to beat on a good day.
searchQuery: picnic Phoenix Park Dublin
availabilityNote: Sun only — grab supplies from a deli first

title: South William Street Brunch
description: The stretch from South William Street down to Drury Street is Dublin's best for weekend brunch — Listons, Paulie's Pizza, General Merchants and more all within a few minutes.
searchQuery: South William Street brunch Dublin
availabilityNote: Weekend mornings — expect queues at the good spots

title: Powerscourt Gardens
description: One of the great gardens of Ireland — formal terraces, a Japanese garden, a pets' cemetery, and views to Sugar Loaf mountain. About 30 minutes from Dublin. Worth every minute of the drive.

title: Powerscourt Waterfall
description: Ireland's highest waterfall in a beautiful forest setting with picnic areas. A short drive from the gardens or a lovely standalone trip from Dublin. Spectacular after heavy rain.

title: Glendalough Monastic Site & Lakes
description: Ancient monastic ruins beside two glacial lakes in the heart of the Wicklow Mountains. One of Ireland's most visited sites and deservedly so — genuinely stunning in any weather.
availabilityNote: Arrive early — parking fills on weekends

title: Wicklow Mountains National Park
description: Drive 45 minutes south to wild moorland, glacial valleys, and total silence. The Sally Gap, Luggala, and the Military Road are all extraordinary. Bring layers regardless of the forecast.
availabilityNote: Car needed — changeable weather, plan layers

title: Hell Fire Club, Montpelier Hill
description: A short but steep climb in the Dublin Mountains to a ruined 18th-century hunting lodge with a mythic reputation and sweeping city views from the top. One of Dublin's best-kept secrets.
availabilityNote: Short steep climb — city panorama at the top

title: Killruddery House & Gardens
description: A 17th-century estate in Bray with formal gardens, a working farm, and one of Ireland's best garden cafés. Seasonal markets make it worth the trip any time of year.
availabilityNote: Seasonal markets and café on site

title: Trim Castle Day Trip
description: The largest Anglo-Norman castle in Ireland, on the banks of the Boyne in County Meath. About an hour from Dublin — a genuine day trip with a riverside walk, ruins, and great history.

title: Mulligan's of Poolbeg Street
description: Arguably the finest Guinness in Dublin since 1782. Dark, unchanged, and utterly serious about its pint. No frills, no music, no tourists who know what they're doing. Just perfection.
searchQuery: Mulligan's pub Poolbeg Street Dublin Guinness

title: Kehoe's, South Anne Street
description: One of Dublin's best-preserved Victorian pubs. Snugs, original fittings, and a Guinness that rewards patience. Gets busy but never loses its soul.
searchQuery: Kehoe's pub South Anne Street Dublin Guinness

title: Doheny & Nesbitt
description: A Baggot Street institution beloved by politicians, journalists, and anyone who knows a good pint. The snug at the back is one of Dublin's great spots.
searchQuery: Doheny and Nesbitt pub Baggot Street Dublin Guinness

title: The Stag's Head
description: A jaw-dropping Victorian interior on Dame Court — stained glass, marble, mounted stag. The Guinness matches the surroundings. A Dublin essential that never disappoints.
searchQuery: Stag's Head pub Dame Court Dublin Guinness

title: Toner's, Baggot Street
description: Unchanged since the 1800s, with wooden drawers behind the bar that once held grocery orders. The Guinness is excellent. Yeats drank here. That's all you need to know.
searchQuery: Toner's pub Baggot Street Dublin Guinness

title: The Long Hall
description: South Great George's Street landmark with an extraordinary Victorian interior — chandeliers, clocks, carved mahogany. The pint is worth the trip alone. One of Ireland's great pub interiors.
searchQuery: The Long Hall pub Dublin Guinness

title: Grogan's Castle Lounge
description: A South William Street bohemian institution. Writers, artists, and people who take their Guinness very seriously. Unhurried, unpretentious, and exactly right.
searchQuery: Grogan's Castle Lounge South William Street Dublin Guinness

title: The Palace Bar, Fleet Street
description: One of Dublin's oldest pubs, with a beautiful curved bar and a serious Guinness reputation. Literary history on every wall. A Fleet Street institution since 1823.
searchQuery: Palace Bar Fleet Street Dublin Guinness

title: McDaid's, Harry Street
description: Brendan Behan's local. A tall narrow Victorian pub off Grafton Street with a devoted following and a Guinness that never disappoints. Steps from the shopping crowds, miles from them in spirit.
searchQuery: McDaid's pub Harry Street Dublin Guinness

title: Neary's, Chatham Street
description: A beautifully kept Victorian pub steps from Grafton Street. Polished brass, a warm welcome, and one of the most consistently good pints in the city. Somehow always feels right.
searchQuery: Neary's pub Chatham Street Dublin Guinness
